about: Each species' hunt act and what it follows: a catalogue row (the species' own text), its ambient hunting recipe, or E5's hunt style. Generated by scripts/ark-hunt-acts.mts.

acts.name: African Grey Hornbill
acts.quote: Mostly insects such as grasshoppers and caterpillars, gleaned from branches and sometimes caught in flight, plus small lizards and fruit.

acts.name: African Penguin
acts.quote: It hunts by pursuit diving, usually to less than 30 metres though dives past 100 metres are recorded, and small groups often herd shoals together.

acts.name: Alligator Snapping Turtle
acts.because: clip:tongue_lure_gape: lies jaws-open wriggling a lure
acts.quote: Lying on the river bed with its jaws wide open, the turtle wriggles a pink, worm-shaped flap on its tongue until a fish swims in to take it.

acts.name: American Alligator
acts.quote: The strike is an explosive lunge and bite with one of the strongest measured bite forces of any living animal, lasting seconds, after which the animal returns to stillness.

acts.name: American Bullfrog
acts.because: ambush: waits at the water edge to catch prey
acts.quote: They are large frogs that wait at water edges to catch many types of prey.

acts.name: American Crocodile
acts.quote: Patient ambush style from water edges

acts.name: American Kestrel
acts.quote: A kestrel sitting on a roadside wire drops to the verge and flies back with a grasshopper gripped in one foot, then eats it on the perch.

acts.name: American Toad
acts.because: strike + look:tongue_flick: flicks out a sticky tongue
acts.quote: Prey is caught with a sticky tongue fixed at the front of the mouth, flicked out and back in a fraction of a second.

acts.name: Asian Glossy Starling
acts.quote: Mainly fruit, especially figs, palm fruits and berries, swallowed whole in the canopy, plus nectar and insects such as flying termites caught on the wing.

acts.name: Asian Hornet
acts.quote: The Asian Hornet hovers in front of a beehive like a tiny helicopter, snatches returning honeybees out of the air and carries them home to feed its larvae.

acts.name: Barn Funnel Weaver
acts.because: ambush: sprints from tube, bites prey and drags it back
acts.quote: When an insect blunders onto the sheet, the spider sprints from the tube, bites it and drags it back inside to eat.

acts.name: Barn Owl
acts.because: hover_drop: flies silently, then strikes prey hidden under grass
acts.quote: Barn Owls hunt small mammals (like voles) in complete darkness, often striking prey hidden under vegetation or snow.

acts.name: Barn Swallow
acts.quote: Barn Swallows catch flying insects mid-air, consuming their food while remaining in continuous flight.

acts.name: Bengal Tiger
acts.because: pounce (stalk + ambush): patient lone stalk then explosive finish
acts.quote: They often drag prey to cover after a kill.

acts.name: Black-and-yellow Garden Spider
acts.quote: Grasshoppers, bees, wasps, flies and moths that blunder into the web make up most meals.

acts.name: Black Caiman
acts.quote: Powerful ambush jaws

acts.name: Black-crested Coquette
acts.quote: Beyond nectar, Coquettes also catch tiny insects and spiders in flight.

acts.name: Black-headed Gull
acts.because: clip:foot_paddle: paddles on the spot to bring worms up
acts.quote: On soft mud or in shallow water it treads rapidly on the spot, and worms and small animals rise to the surface to be picked off.

acts.name: Bocage's Wall Lizard
acts.quote: or by a quick dash from a basking spot

acts.name: Bolas Spider
acts.quote: Bolas Spider feeds on male moths attracted by mimicked pheromones and caught with a sticky silk droplet.

acts.name: Bold Jumper
acts.quote: The Bold Jumper creeps close to its prey, anchors a silk line, then jumps and bites.

acts.name: Book Scorpion
acts.quote: Venom glands in its pincers subdue prey, while silk for its moulting chambers comes from glands opening on its jaws.

acts.name: Brahminy Kite
acts.because: talon_grab: soars over water scanning, swoops only when it spots food
acts.quote: From their high vantage point, Brahminy Kites scan large areas of water and land for fish, crabs, small animals, and carrion, swooping down only when an opportunity is identified.

acts.name: Brazilian Lava Lizard
acts.because: pounce: motionless on rock then dashes out at insect
acts.quote: It sits motionless on speckled rock or sand, its grey-brown mottling blending with the surface, until an insect passes and it dashes out.

acts.name: Brown Pelican
acts.because: air_plunge: plunge-dives with folded wings, scoops fish in the pouch
acts.quote: The Brown Pelican uses sharp eyes to spot fish, then folds its wings and drops into the water with its giant pouch-like bill.

acts.name: Brown Shrike
acts.because: pounce (from perch): drops onto insects and lizards
acts.quote: sometimes spikes its catch on a thorn to eat later

acts.name: Brown Widow Spider
acts.quote: Flies, mosquitoes, small beetles, moths and other arthropods caught in an irregular tangle web.

acts.name: Brown Wood Owl
acts.because: pounce: perches silently then swoops down
acts.quote: They often perch silently on a branch, listening and watching intently in low light conditions, before swooping down rapidly and silently to capture unsuspecting prey.

acts.name: Budgett's Frog
acts.quote: The frog's comical look is exactly what makes its ambush design memorable.

acts.name: Buffy Fish Owl
acts.because: talon_grab: perches low over water, drops to snatch fish from the surface
acts.quote: Once prey is detected, the owl drops swiftly and precisely to snatch it from the water surface with its talons.

acts.name: Burgundy Goliath Birdeater
acts.quote: Prey is killed with venom and the fangs, then softened with digestive fluid.

acts.name: Carolina Wolf Spider
acts.because: pounce: chases ground insects, pins them with front legs
acts.quote: At night it leaves its burrow and chases down crickets, beetles and other ground insects, pinning them with its front legs before it bites.

acts.name: Chaco Golden Knee Tarantula
acts.quote: Insects, other invertebrates and occasionally very small vertebrates ambushed at the burrow mouth.

acts.name: Cheetah
acts.quote: It stalks close before sprinting, trips the prey with a forepaw and kills with a suffocating throat bite.

acts.name: Chinese Giant Salamander
acts.quote: Chinese Giant Salamanders are primarily nocturnal ambush predators, waiting patiently for fish, frogs, and other aquatic animals to come within striking distance.

acts.name: Chinese Mantis
acts.because: ambush+strike: stands still and ambushes passing insects
acts.quote: If you want to catch something quickly, try standing still and waiting for the right moment

acts.name: Chinese Pond Heron
acts.quote: A hunting bird crouches motionless at the edge of a paddy or pond for minutes at a time, then shoots its neck out to seize a fish or frog.

acts.name: Chinese Softshell Turtle
acts.quote: Aquatic ambush style from soft freshwater bottoms

acts.name: Cobweb Spider
acts.quote: Irregular cobwebs work differently from neat orb webs

acts.name: Common Blackbird
acts.quote: Runs or hops across grass, then stops with head tilted

acts.name: Common Bluetail
acts.quote: Males perch on low stems at the water's edge and dart out to seize tiny flies and midges, returning to the same reed again and again.

acts.name: Common Buzzard
acts.because: hover: hangs almost motionless in the wind
acts.quote: In a steady wind over a ridge it hangs almost motionless, trimming its tail and wingtips while it watches the grass below.

acts.name: Common Darter
acts.quote: Repeatedly returns to the same sun-warmed perch after hunting flights.

acts.name: Common Flangetail
acts.quote: A common flangetail sits on the tip of a stick above a pond for a long time, then darts out to grab a passing fly and lands back on the same stick.

acts.name: Common Frog
acts.quote: Adults eat slugs, snails, worms, beetles, flies, spiders and other small invertebrates, snapped up with a sticky tongue from a sit-and-wait ambush.

acts.name: Common House Gecko
acts.quote: Common House Geckos frequently hunt insects attracted to artificial lights on walls and ceilings of human dwellings at night.

acts.name: Common House Spider
acts.quote: named for a row of serrated bristles on the hind legs used to fling silk over prey

acts.name: Common Kestrel
acts.because: hover_drop: hovers with head perfectly still, then drops on a vole
acts.quote: A kestrel hangs in the wind over a grassy field, wings fluttering fast while its head stays perfectly still as it watches for a vole.

acts.name: Common Kingfisher
acts.because: perch_plunge: perches still above water then dives in a flash for fish
acts.quote: Still perching above water before sudden dives

acts.name: Common Snapping Turtle
acts.quote: Their rhythm is wait in mud, sense movement, snap when needed

acts.name: Common Wall Gecko
acts.quote: On warm nights it stations itself beside outdoor lamps on house walls, clinging motionless until a moth lands within reach.

acts.name: Crab Spider
acts.quote: Bees, flies, moths, and other insects captured by ambush.

acts.name: Crested Serpent Eagle
acts.because: pounce: watches the floor from a shaded perch, drops on snakes
acts.quote: The eagle hunts from a shaded perch below the canopy, watching the forest floor for movement, rather than quartering the ground in flight.

acts.name: Crimson Sunbird
acts.quote: Nectar from flowers such as hibiscus, banana, coral trees and mistletoes, taken while perched or in brief hovering, plus small insects and spiders picked from foliage or caught in flight.

acts.name: Daddy Long-Legs Spider
acts.quote: It creeps into another spider's web and plucks the threads to imitate trapped prey, then kills the owner when it comes to investigate.

acts.name: Darwin’s Bark Spider
acts.quote: Orb web hung in open air over water, not among foliage

acts.name: Devil's Flower Mantis
acts.quote: ambush arms

acts.name: Domestic Cat
acts.quote: Crouched motionless beside a gap in a fence, a cat may wait for many minutes, then pounce in under a second when a mouse appears.

acts.name: Dragonfly
acts.quote: Larvae ambush tadpoles, small fish and aquatic insects by shooting out a hinged lower lip tipped with hooks.

acts.name: Dwarf Caiman
acts.quote: Still-water ambush behavior in forest creeks

acts.name: Eastern Phoebe
acts.quote: often returning to the same perch after each short insect-catching flight.

acts.name: Eurasian Eagle-Owl
acts.because: pounce: silent approach and powerful talon strike
acts.quote: The owl flies silently, approaching prey undetected, and strikes with powerful talons for a swift, conclusive capture.

acts.name: European Hornet
acts.quote: The European Hornet hunts on into the night, drawn to lit windows, when other wasps have long stopped.

acts.name: False Gharial
acts.quote: Ambush strategy in swampy rivers and peatlands

acts.name: Flower Crab Spider
acts.because: clip:crab_spider_leg_clamp: waits on a flower with front legs open
acts.quote: A female waits motionless on a flower head with her long front legs held open, then clamps them shut on a bee or butterfly that lands to feed.

acts.name: Giant Asian Mantis
acts.because: pose:leaf_sway: sways like a leaf while watching prey
acts.quote: While watching an insect draw near, it is often seen swaying gently from side to side on its perch like a leaf stirred by a breeze.

acts.name: Giant Dead Leaf Mantis
acts.quote: An ambush predator that waits motionless and snatches passing insects such as flies, moths and crickets with its spiny forelegs.

acts.name: Giant Golden Orb-weaver
acts.quote: Flying insects caught in the web, including moths, beetles, flies, cicadas and grasshoppers.

acts.name: Giant House Spider
acts.because: ambush: waits motionless in funnel, dashes out on vibration
acts.quote: Upon detecting vibrations, the spider dashes out of its retreat at remarkable speed to capture the prey.

acts.name: Giant Leaf-tailed Gecko
acts.quote: It hunts mostly by waiting on a trunk or branch and lunging at prey that moves within reach.

acts.name: Giant Water Bug
acts.quote: Powerful raptorial forelegs seize prey in aquatic ambushes.

acts.name: Golden Silk Orb-weaver
acts.quote: Small silvery spiders of the genus Argyrodes often live in the web and steal wrapped prey.

acts.name: Great Blue Heron
acts.quote: The folded neck stores speed for a sudden forward strike.

acts.name: Great Cormorant
acts.quote: Great Cormorants dive from the surface, propelling themselves with strong feet and streamlined bodies to pursue fish, often bottom-dwelling species, using a hooked bill to secure prey.

acts.name: Great Egret
acts.quote: Their S-shaped neck straightens quickly during a strike.

acts.name: Great Kiskadee
acts.quote: Attacks are brief outward flights from the perch to the prey and straight back, rather than sustained pursuit or patrolling.

acts.name: Great Plains Toad
acts.quote: A sit-and-wait and wandering feeder that takes beetles, ants, caterpillars and other ground insects.

acts.name: Greater Bulldog Bat
acts.quote: Fish are chewed on the wing and stored in cheek pouches, so the bat can keep hunting before it lands to finish eating.

acts.name: Grey Heron
acts.quote: When prey comes within striking distance, the heron extends its neck with lightning speed and impales or grasps the prey with its sharp bill, often with remarkable accuracy.

acts.name: Happy-face Spider
acts.quote: It spins a sparse web of a few threads beneath a leaf, rests against the leaf surface and runs out to seize prey that touches the lines.

acts.name: Harvestman
acts.quote: They can vibrate rapidly in their webs to confuse predators.

acts.name: Hellbender
acts.quote: Low-profile ambush and shelter strategy

acts.name: Horned Sungem
acts.quote: Nectar from small flowers of shrubs and herbs, taken while hovering, together with small insects caught in flight or picked from foliage.

acts.name: House Centipede
acts.quote: At night it races across walls and floors, stopping dead before rushing a silverfish or cockroach.

acts.name: Humboldt Penguin
acts.quote: It hunts by sight in pursuit dives, mostly within a few tens of metres of the surface, and usually feeds within a day's swim of the colony while raising chicks.

acts.name: Huntsman Spider
acts.quote: They ambush or rush prey, pin it with the front legs and subdue it with a venomous bite.

acts.name: Indochinese Tiger
acts.because: pounce: silent stalk then short powerful attack
acts.quote: After a silent stalk, the tiger waits for the opportune moment, then launches a sudden, powerful, short-distance attack.

acts.name: Javan Pond Heron
acts.quote: Short legs keep it to very shallow water, and it often hunts from floating plants, banks or the low walls between rice paddies.

acts.name: Jumping Spider
acts.quote: Before pouncing, jumping spiders often stalk their prey, moving slowly and pausing to re-evaluate their position and the target's movement.

acts.name: King Penguin
acts.quote: Powerful underwater pursuit diving for fish and squid.

acts.name: Komodo Dragon
acts.quote: Komodo dragons are ambush predators, waiting concealed for prey like deer and pigs to come within striking distance.

acts.name: Kuhl's Pipistrelle Bat
acts.quote: Closing on a moth, a Kuhl's pipistrelle speeds up its calls until they run together in a rapid buzz.

acts.name: Ladybird Spider
acts.quote: Prey that blunders into the sheet of woolly, sticky silk around the burrow mouth becomes entangled and is dragged underground.

acts.name: Laughing Kookaburra
acts.because: pounce: perches still then swoops to pounce on ground prey
acts.quote: Perch-and-Pounce Hunting: stillness on a branch becomes sudden ground action.

acts.name: Leopard Gecko
acts.quote: making it a ground hunter that waits at burrow mouths for passing insects

acts.name: Lesser Adjutant Stork
acts.quote: It usually hunts alone, walking slowly through shallow water and mud and stabbing at prey it has seen.

acts.name: Lesser Banded Hornet
acts.quote: Colonies hunt honey bees at hive entrances

acts.name: Little Black Cormorant
acts.quote: Little black cormorants line up across a lake and dive one after another, so fish trying to escape one bird swim straight to the next.

acts.name: Little Blue Heron
acts.quote: After a period of stillness or slow movement, the heron will suddenly and quickly stab its bill into the water to capture its prey.

acts.name: Little Egret
acts.quote: The egret dashes through shallows with wings partly spread, changing direction abruptly, and takes fish as they are forced toward the shallowest margins.

acts.name: Little Owl
acts.because: pounce: watches from a fence post, glides down onto voles and beetles
acts.quote: From a fence post at twilight it watches the grass below, then glides down onto a vole or beetle it has picked out by sight and sound.

acts.name: Long-jawed Orb Weaver
acts.quote: Orb web with open hub in many species

acts.name: Longhorned Orbweaver
acts.quote: It is placed in Gasteracanthinae, the spiny orb-weaver subfamily of the orb-web family Araneidae.

acts.name: Marbled Orbweaver
acts.quote: Flying insects such as flies, moths, midges and small beetles caught in a vertical orb web.

acts.name: Marvellous Spatuletail
acts.quote: Nectar taken while hovering at tubular flowers, with Bomarea climbers among the plants it has been recorded visiting, plus small insects snatched in flight or gleaned from foliage.

acts.name: Masked Water Tyrant
acts.quote: It walks along the edge of a pond and across floating plants, stopping to pick insects from the surface

acts.name: Mata Mata
acts.quote: They are poor active swimmers compared with many turtles, relying on still ambush.

acts.name: Mediterranean House Gecko
acts.quote: On warm nights it waits beside outdoor lamps and darts out to snap up moths and other insects that the light draws in.

acts.name: minute pirate bug
acts.because: ambush: waits among flower parts and grabs prey that comes close
acts.quote: It sits among flower parts and leaf veins until a thrips or aphid moves close, then grabs it and drives its beak in.

acts.name: Mirror Spider
acts.quote: Comb-footed spiders use the row of bristles on the hind legs to draw out sticky silk and fling it over struggling prey.

acts.name: Mugger Crocodile
acts.because: ambush+strike: ambush at drinking spots then sudden lunge
acts.quote: They consistently choose ambush sites near common prey access points like drinking spots, river crossings, or narrow channels.

acts.name: Neotropic Cormorant
acts.quote: The Neotropic Cormorant uses a hooked bill and strong feet to chase fish underwater, then spreads its wings wide to dry.

acts.name: Orb-weaver Spider
acts.quote: Many orb-weavers hide in a curled leaf beside the web holding a signal thread, and drop to the ground on a safety line when disturbed.

acts.name: Orchid Mantis
acts.because: ambush+strike: waits on vegetation looking like a flower
acts.quote: Orchid mantises are famous for flower-like mimicry, and experiments showed insects approached them more often than real flowers.

acts.name: Oriental Garden Lizard
acts.quote: The lizard commonly hunts visually from a perch, observing its surroundings before making a short, rapid attack on prey.

acts.name: Orinoco Mata Mata Turtle
acts.quote: It waits for prey to come close, then opens its wide mouth and expands its throat, sucking the victim in with a rush of water and swallowing it whole.

acts.name: Ornate Horned Frog
acts.quote: Very large mouth used for sudden ambush strikes.

acts.name: Osprey
acts.because: air_plunge: plunges feet-first into water to seize fish
acts.quote: The bird plunges feet-first, closes its nostrils on entry, and has dense oily plumage that prevents waterlogging, unlike cormorants which must dry out.

acts.name: Pantropical Jumping Spider
acts.because: pounce: walks into range on a sunny wall, then jumps
acts.quote: The Pantropical Jumping Spider walks into range on a wall, then jumps.

acts.name: Peacock Spider
acts.quote: It hunts by sight, stalking small insects, other spiders and tiny arthropods across leaves and ground litter, then leaping onto them while attached to a silk safety line.

acts.name: Peacock Tarantula
acts.quote: Large insects such as crickets, cockroaches and moths, seized in a quick ambush at night as they pass close by.

acts.name: Peregrine Falcon
acts.quote: The peregrine climbs to a position high above its prey and then stoops with wings folded, reaching speeds far beyond what any flapping flight could produce.

acts.name: Peters's Jumping Spider
acts.quote: Before leaping it attaches a silk safety line to the surface, so a missed jump ends dangling rather than falling.

acts.name: Pied Butcherbird
acts.because: pounce (perch-return): launches at prey, returns to lookout
acts.quote: It watches from an exposed perch, launches when prey reveals itself and returns to a useful lookout.

acts.name: Pied Fantail
acts.quote: Once an insect is in the air it gives chase with the tail spread, twisting and looping between the branches before it returns to a perch.

acts.name: Praying Mantis
acts.quote: Praying mantises are ambush predators with spiny grasping forelegs.

acts.name: Racket-tailed Roller
acts.because: pounce: watches from a perch then drops to seize prey on the ground
acts.quote: The Racket-tailed Roller watches from a perch, often within the canopy, before dropping to the ground to seize its prey.

acts.name: Red Assassin Bug
acts.because: ambush: waits on stems to seize passing insects
acts.quote: The Assassin Bug uses sticky grasping legs and a sharp beak to wait on stems until another insect wanders too close.

acts.name: Red Fox
acts.because: clip:fox_mouse_pounce: high arcing pounce onto prey heard under grass/snow
acts.quote: The fox's large ears and acute low-frequency hearing allow it to locate rodents moving beneath grass, leaf litter and snow, after which it makes a high arcing pounce onto the detected point.

acts.name: Red-kneed Tarantula
acts.because: prop:burrow_entrance: sits at the entrance after dark
acts.quote: The day is spent inside the burrow, often behind a thin curtain of silk. After dark it sits at the entrance waiting for prey to pass

acts.name: Red-tailed Hawk
acts.because: perch+scan+dive_air: a steep stoop onto prey
acts.quote: The hawk does not flush or chase speculatively; it waits until prey is visually located and then launches a direct stoop onto it.

acts.name: Red-veined Darter
acts.quote: A male launches from a reed tip, twists sharply in mid-air to snatch a passing midge, and returns to the same perch within seconds.

acts.name: Ring-billed Gull
acts.because: aerial_hawk: hawks swarms of mayflies and flying ants
acts.quote: Flocks follow a tractor across a field and drop behind the plough to seize the worms and grubs it turns up.

acts.name: Rivoli's Hummingbird
acts.quote: It also eats many small insects and spiders, gleaned from leaves or snapped from the air.

acts.name: Roadside Hawk
acts.because: pounce: drops from a low post onto prey and flies back up
acts.quote: From a low post it watches the grass below, drops onto a grasshopper, lizard or mouse, and flies back up to wait again.

acts.name: Ruddy Darter
acts.quote: A male waits on a stem or twig overlooking open water, darts out after a gnat or a rival, and usually settles back on the same perch within seconds.

acts.name: Saddle-billed Stork
acts.quote: Saddle-billed Storks hunt by walking slowly and deliberately through shallow water, often standing motionless for extended periods before striking with precision.

acts.name: Saltwater Crocodile
acts.because: ambush+strike: log-like submerged waiting then explosive strike
acts.quote: Saltwater Crocodiles spend hours, often days, submerged or partially submerged, appearing almost like logs, waiting for prey to approach.

acts.name: Serval
acts.because: clip:serval_high_pounce: listens, then high pounce onto hidden rodents
acts.quote: Their pounce can be high enough to catch birds or drop onto hidden rodents.

acts.name: Siamese Crocodile
acts.because: ambush+strike: submerged stillness then sudden lunge
acts.quote: Siamese Crocodiles remain largely submerged and still in freshwater, waiting for prey to come within striking distance, then execute a sudden, powerful lunge.

acts.name: Slender Skimmer
acts.quote: Adults hunt small flying insects on the wing and are also reported to catch and eat other dragonflies.

acts.name: Snowy Egret
acts.quote: Snowy egrets extend a bright yellow foot into shallow water and mud and vibrate, shuffle or rake it, then strike at the prey that breaks cover in response.

acts.name: Southern Black Widow
acts.quote: Insects and other small arthropods that stumble into its low tangled web, such as beetles, crickets, cockroaches and woodlice.

acts.name: Spectacled Caiman
acts.because: clip:caiman_side_snap: drifts with eyes and nostrils above water
acts.quote: After dark it drifts with only its eyes and nostrils above the water, then snaps sideways at fish that swim within reach.

acts.name: Spiny Flower Mantis
acts.quote: It waits motionless on or near a bloom and snatches prey with its spined front legs.

acts.name: Spinybacked Orbweaver
acts.quote: Spiny Orb-weaver feeds on small flies, mosquitoes, moths, wasps, and other insects trapped in orb webs.

acts.name: Spotted Wood Owl
acts.because: pounce: perches motionless listening, then a short silent descent
acts.quote: The attack is a short, direct descent from the perch, with strong talons taking the prey at the end, and the owl returns to a perch rather than pursuing a miss.

acts.name: Stick Mantis
acts.because: ambush+strike: forelegs folded and still until prey comes within reach
acts.quote: It is thought to hold its forelegs folded and still for long periods, relying on its twig-like shape until prey comes within reach.

acts.name: Sumatran Tiger
acts.because: pounce: gets very close undetected then sudden attack
acts.quote: Sumatran Tigers are ambush predators, relying on getting very close to their prey undetected before launching a sudden, powerful attack.

acts.name: Surinam Horned Frog
acts.quote: Wide mouth built for sudden ambush feeding.

acts.name: Texas Unicorn Mantis
acts.quote: It waits motionless on a stem and snatches prey with its spined front legs.

acts.name: Tiger Wolf Spider
acts.because: ambush: waits motionless, then runs prey down in a short dash
acts.quote: Larger individuals of the same species sometimes eat smaller ones.

acts.name: Tomato Frog
acts.quote: An ambush hunter that sits still and snaps up whatever comes within reach: mainly beetles, crickets and other insects, with worms and other small invertebrates.

acts.name: Trapdoor Spider
acts.quote: The trapdoor strategy saves energy by making prey come close first.

acts.name: Trashline Orb-weaver
acts.quote: Orb web is small, with closely spaced spiral threads

acts.name: Tree Frog
acts.quote: Adults eat flies, moths, crickets, beetles, ants, spiders and other small invertebrates, caught with a flick of the sticky tongue or a lunge from a perch.

acts.name: Triangulate Combfoot
acts.quote: Small crawling arthropods caught in its irregular web, including ants, beetles, woodlice, ticks and other spiders.

acts.name: Tricolored Heron
acts.quote: The Tricolored Heron wades up to its white belly in the shallows, sometimes standing still and sometimes dashing with wings half open before spearing a small fish with its long thin bill.

acts.name: Tropical House Gecko
acts.quote: The Tropical House Gecko settles on the wall beside a lamp after dark and snaps up the insects that the light draws in.

acts.name: Two-striped Telamonia
acts.quote: A Two-striped Telamonia creeps across a leaf toward a fly, ties on a thin silk safety line, then leaps onto it in one quick jump.

acts.name: Variable Hawk
acts.quote: Mostly rodents such as leaf-eared mice and tuco-tucos, and introduced rabbits in parts of Patagonia; it also takes small birds, lizards, snakes, beetles and grasshoppers, usually seized on the ground after a short stoop.

acts.name: Walnut Orb-weaver
acts.quote: A signal thread runs from the hub of its web to its hiding place, and vibrations along that line tell it when an insect has been caught.

acts.name: Wasp Spider
acts.quote: Grasshoppers and crickets are the main prey, with flies, bees and other insects that jump or fly into the low web.

acts.name: Wheel Bug
acts.because: stalk+strike: strikes when prey comes in range
acts.quote: slowly patrolling vegetation and striking when prey comes within range

acts.name: White-bellied Sea Eagle
acts.because: talon_grab: dives and snatches prey from the surface
acts.quote: After spotting prey (fish, sea snakes, birds, etc.) from a distance, the eagle executes a precise dive, often snatching the target with strong talons from the water's surface or shore.

acts.name: White-throated Kingfisher
acts.because: pounce: drops from a wire or branch onto lizards, crabs and insects
acts.quote: The White-throated Kingfisher often hunts far from water, dropping from a wire or branch onto lizards, frogs, crabs and large insects as well as fish.

acts.name: Woodlouse Hunter Spider
acts.quote: The spider pins a woodlouse with one fang on its armored back while driving the other into the soft underside.

acts.name: Yacare Caiman
acts.quote: Ambush feeding on fish, invertebrates, and small vertebrates.

acts.name: Yellow-legged Gull
acts.because: mixed_follow: snatches discarded fish astern of trawlers
acts.quote: Yellow-legged Gulls frequently follow fishing boats, especially trawlers, to feed on discarded bycatch and fish disturbed by the nets.

acts.name: Yellow Sac Spider
acts.quote: At night it roams grass stems and leaves, seizing insects and other small arthropods and subduing them with a quick venomous bite.
